I give up. I could not find a proof I could formalize, so I have not edited `/work/putnam_2004_b6.lean`.

What I established:

- **The statement is not vacuous.** If `A` is infinite, its difference set is infinite, so `b` exists. The hypotheses are consistent and the theorem is the real Putnam 2004 B6 problem.
- **The easy direction works.** If `(n, n+r]` contains no element of `B`, then any block of `n+r` consecutive integers contains at most `n+1` elements of `A`. This gives density at most `(n+1)/(n+r)`, so the bound is small when `r ≫ n`.
- **The gap is at an uncontrolled position.** The hypothesis gives a gap of length `r` at some position `n_r`, but nothing guarantees `n_r = O(r)`. When `n_r ≫ r`, the block bound is useless. I could not close this case.

Formalizing the full argument would also require a substantial amount of Mathlib work on counting and limits, so I stopped here.

I give up.
